title: What the Lord requires (Micah 6:8)
hookLine: to do judgment, to love mercy, and to walk solicitous with thy God

lines: MY PEOPLE, WHAT HAVE I DONE TO THEE?
cards: Micah, called the Morasthite after his hometown, preached in the days of the same kings as Isaiah, and in chapter six he stages a trial.

God takes his people to court, with the mountains and the foundations of the earth as the jury. Then God speaks first, and it isn't an accusation. It's a question: my people, what have I done to thee?
How have I been a burden to you? Answer me. On Good Friday that line is the heart of the Reproaches, chanted while the cross is venerated: in Latin, popule meus, quid feci tibi.

teach.h: THOUSANDS OF RAMS, RIVERS OF OIL?
teach.b: The people answer, and you can feel them getting nervous. What should I bring? Burnt offerings?
Calves a year old? Thousands of rams, many thousands of fat goats, or, as the Hebrew has it, rivers of oil? Should I give my firstborn for my sin?
Each offer is bigger than the last, until it becomes unthinkable.

Then the prophet cuts through it, in the Douay-Rheims: "I will shew thee, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requireth of thee: Verily, to do judgment, and to love mercy, and to walk solicitous with thy God."

teach.h: O MAN: ADAM, ANY HUMAN BEING.
teach.b: O man: in Hebrew, adam, any human being, not just one nation. And three things, none of them expensive. Do judgment: act justly, Amos's word yesterday.
Love mercy: the Hebrew is chesed, the steady loyal love met in Ruth; not just merciful acts now and then, but loving it. The third is the strangest.
The Hebrew is hatznea lechet, and the first word is unusual and hard to pin down; translators reach for modestly, carefully, attentively.

teach.h: JUSTICE, CHESED, AND A CAREFUL WALK.
teach.b: The Latin made it solicitous, so the Douay says walk solicitous: careful, the way you walk beside someone you don't want to lose. The King James says walk humbly, the way the line is often quoted.

teach.h: SOLICITOUS OR HUMBLY: ONE HARD WORD.
teach.b: Both are trying to catch one hard word. Notice the verb, too: walk.

teach.h: WHAT THE LORD REQUIRETH OF THEE.
teach.b: Not arrive. A walk is daily, one step after another, and it's done with someone. The people offered rivers of oil.
God asked for a way of walking.

how: On Good Friday the Church chants the Reproaches, built on Micah 6:3, during the veneration of the cross, and Micah 6:8 is quoted in Catholic teaching on justice and mercy.

o: walking in a long procession to the Temple
bringing rivers of oil as an offering

s: Micah says God wants bigger and better offerings
the people offer more and more; Micah answers with three things that cost nothing: justice, mercy and a careful walk.
the Good Friday Reproaches echo a line from Micah
my people, what have I done to thee? from Micah 6:3.
walk solicitous and walk humbly translate the same rare Hebrew word
hatznea: modestly, carefully. the Latin gave solicitous, the King James humbly.

games.q: you're in God's courtroom with the mountains as jury. you want to make things right. what do you offer?
o: thousands of rams and ten thousand rivers of oil.
to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.
games.why: Micah cuts through the bidding war: I will shew thee, O man, what is good. three things, none of them expensive.

practice: Say the three over slowly, do justly, love mercy, walk humbly, and notice which one tugs at you: something unfair to set right, someone to be kind to steadily, or a walk that's been a little too loud and sure.
Pick just one, and picture the moment you'll live it. If you pray, offer that one step to God.

wordCard.voice: hatznea lechet. Hebrew for walking carefully with God: Micah's third requirement, after doing justice and loving mercy. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: to walk modestly or carefully. the first word is unusual; the Latin has solicitous, the King James humbly.

carryVoice: Your line: walk humbly. Justly, mercifully, and carefully, with God beside you. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: I will shew thee, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requireth of thee: Verily, to do judgment, and to love mercy, and to walk solicitous with thy God.
